title: Brookfield, NextEra to Build $100 Billion AI Hub on Cold War Nuclear Site
key_facts: The US Department of Energy announced a $100 billion private investment to turn the former uranium enrichment site in Western Kentucky into the Paducah American Energy Hub, led by Energy Secretary Chris Wright.
Brookfield Asset Management will build a 1.8 GW AI and high-performance computing campus.
NextEra Energy will develop 2 GW of gas-fired generation and 2.6 GW of battery storage.
Phased buildout targeted for 2032; about 8,000 construction jobs and 600 permanent jobs.
Design meant to feed excess energy back to the regional grid and use closed-loop cooling.
Article says Oracle's $18 billion Project Jupiter in New Mexico has stalled and OpenAI paused Stargate UK in April.
quote_evidence: The phased buildout is targeted for 2032, and is expected to create roughly 8,000 construction jobs and 600 permanent operations jobs.
Still, the Paducah project comes at a time when the market is souring on heavy AI infrastructure spending.
why_it_matters_hint: A very large energy-and-computing project, announced into a nervous market.
notes: One outlet read; DoE statement not seen.
